questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biodiversity and Its Loss' refers to.
questions.a: We share the planet with millions of living beings from micro-organisms and lichens to banyan trees, elephants and blue whales; this biodiversity is threatened as species vanish fastest today - through habitat destruction, hunting, poaching, over-exploitation, environmental pollution and forest fires.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biodiversity and Its Loss'.
questions.a: Species vanish faster now than ever before - and the causes are human.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conservation of Forests and Wildlife' refers to.
questions.a: Conservation safeguards the dwindling variety: the Indian Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 created schedules of protected species, national parks and sanctuaries, and projects like Project Tiger - while newer approaches involve local communities in Joint Forest Management so that protection and livelihoods go together.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conservation of Forests and Wildlife'.
questions.a: Protect by law, involve by livelihood: acts, parks and Joint Forest Management together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conservation of Forests and Wildlife' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: jess102.txt sections on conservation of forests and wildlife)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types and Distribution of Forests' refers to.
questions.a: Forests are classified by management into reserved forests, protected forests and unclassed forests; India's forest cover is judged against the target of one-third of land area, and distribution varies sharply across states and regions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types and Distribution of Forests'.
questions.a: Reserved, protected, unclassed: management status decides how safely a forest lives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types and Distribution of Forests' taught, and from which source text?
